effects: Takes exactly `assets` USDC from the signer and sends it to the vault, using the signer's USDC allowance to the vault.
Mints bbqUSDC vault shares to `onBehalf`. The contract works out the share count (previewDeposit) after accruing fees, and there is no minimum.
If a liquidity adapter is set, forwards the deposited USDC from the vault to the adapter. This is vault-internal and moves none of the signer's funds.
formats.shown: Deposit an exact amount of USDC, with bbqUSDC shares sent to the onBehalf address. The number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit: the number of bbqUSDC shares received is not shown; the contract computes it and sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. Shares are not in the calldata. Case 0: 0.01 bbqUSDC (1e16) minted to the signer. The screen shows only 'Share ticker: bbqUSDC'.
findings.fix: None possible from calldata. The 'Share ticker' line could be relabelled 'Receive shares (bbqUSDC)' so it is clear shares arrive.

cases.notes: The 0.01 USDC out is shown exactly. The asset and recipient of the bbqUSDC shares are shown, but not the amount (1e16), and no descriptor can show it.

effects: Takes USDC from the signer and sends it to the vault, using the signer's USDC allowance. The amount is previewMint(shares), rounded up and computed on chain. It is not in the calldata and has no maximum.
If a liquidity adapter is set, forwards the USDC from the vault to the adapter. This is vault-internal.
formats.shown: Mint an exact number of bbqUSDC to onBehalf, with 'Deposit asset: USDC' as a constant. The USDC amount paid is not shown.

findings.title: mint: the USDC amount taken from the signer is computed on chain and has no maximum, so it is not shown.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint(): `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. enter(): `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: 1.032149 USDC left the signer. The screen shows only 'Deposit asset: USDC'.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds this amount. The descriptor could add a label or note that the USDC cost is set by the current share price.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' and the sentence 'Mint {shares} for {onBehalf}' never say the signer pays USDC.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint: intent 'Mint', interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. The payment shows only as a raw constant field 'Deposit asset: USDC'. Case 1 screen: 'Mint 0.999999999 bbqUSDC for 0x…dEaD'.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Deposit USDC' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Pay USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The signer's only effect is 1.032149 USDC out. The screen names USDC but not the amount, so the reader knew USDC leaves but not how much. The shares went to 0xdead (signer null), and the screen shows that correctly.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns bbqUSDC shares from `onBehalf`. The amount is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up and computed on chain, with no maximum.
When the caller is not `onBehalf`, spends onBehalf's share allowance to the caller by the number of shares burned.
May pull liquidity from the vault's liquidity adapter first. This is vault-internal.
formats.shown: Withdraw an exact amount of USDC to the receiver, from the owner's position. The number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of bbqUSDC shares burned is computed on chain and has no maximum, so it is not shown.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`. exit(): `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 2: 994.200955757341393697 bbqUSDC burned from the signer, and no field shows it.

cases.notes: The 1000 USDC arriving at the signer is shown exactly. The burn of 994.2 bbqUSDC is implied but its amount is not shown, and no descriptor can show it.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` bbqUSDC from `onBehalf`, spending the caller's share allowance when the caller is not onBehalf.
Sends USDC to `receiver`. The amount is previewRedeem(shares), rounded down and computed on chain, with no minimum.
May pull liquidity from the vault's liquidity adapter first. This is vault-internal.
formats.shown: Redeem an exact number of bbqUSDC shares to the receiver, from the owner's position. Neither the asset received nor its amount is shown.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says USDC is received; other formats show it as a constant, this one does not.
findings.evidence: descriptor redeem fields: 'Shares to redeem', 'To', 'Owner' only. mint has a constant field `$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker`. Case 3: 1 USDC arrived at the signer. The reader wrote 'Which token is paid out; I'm assuming USDC from the name'.
findings.fix: Add a field `{label: 'Receive asset', value: '$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker', format: 'raw'}` and use 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is computed on chain and has no minimum, so it is not shown.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. Case 3: 1.000000 USDC was received, and no field shows it.

cases.notes: The 0.9957 bbqUSDC out is shown exactly. The USDC that arrived appears neither by asset nor by amount; the reader guessed USDC.

redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver,.worst: redeem: the screen never says USDC is received; other formats show it as a constant, this one does not.
